assumptions.description: Assume $f:\mathbb R^{d_x}\times\mathbb R^{d_y}\to\mathbb R$. Both blocks are unconstrained and use Euclidean norms. The joint gradient satisfies $\|\nabla f(z)-\nabla f(w)\|_2\le \beta\|z-w\|_2$.
assumptions.scope: The complete stated domain. Constants remain uniform when the other variable block is fixed.

assumptions.description: The condition $f\in C^2$ holds, and the full joint Hessian satisfies $\|\nabla^2f(z)-\nabla^2f(w)\|_{\rm op}\le\rho\|z-w\|_2$.
assumptions.scope: The complete stated domain. Constants remain uniform when the other variable block is fixed.

assumptions.description: For every $x$, $f(x,\cdot)$ is uniformly $\mu_y$-strongly concave. Thus $y^\star(x)=\arg\max_y f(x,y)$ is unique and $\Phi(x)=f(x,y^\star(x))$ is differentiable. Neither $f(\cdot,y)$ nor $\Phi$ is assumed convex.
assumptions.scope: The complete stated domain. Constants remain uniform when the other variable block is fixed.

assumptions.description: Assume $\inf_x\Phi(x)>-\infty$, with an initial point satisfying $\Phi(x_0)-\inf_x\Phi(x)\le\Delta$.
assumptions.scope: The complete stated domain. Constants remain uniform when the other variable block is fixed.

assumptions.description: The public initial point additionally satisfies $\|y_0-y^\star(x_0)\|_2\le R_y$. The condition number is $\kappa=\beta/\mu_y$.
assumptions.scope: The complete stated domain. Constants remain uniform when the other variable block is fixed.

description_paragraphs: $f:\mathbb{R}^{d_x}\times\mathbb{R}^{d_y}\to\mathbb{R}$, with both blocks unconstrained and Euclidean norms throughout. The joint gradient satisfies $\|\nabla f(z)-\nabla f(w)\|_2\le \beta\|z-w\|_2$.
The condition $f\in C^2$ holds, and the full joint Hessian satisfies $\|\nabla^2f(z)-\nabla^2f(w)\|_{\rm op}\le\rho\|z-w\|_2$.

For every $x$, $f(x,\cdot)$ is uniformly $\mu_y$-strongly concave. Thus $y^\star(x)=\arg\max_y f(x,y)$ is unique and $\Phi(x)=f(x,y^\star(x))$ is differentiable. Neither $f(\cdot,y)$ nor $\Phi$ is assumed convex.
Assume $\inf_x\Phi(x)>-\infty$, with an initial point satisfying $\Phi(x_0)-\inf_x\Phi(x)\le\Delta$.
The public initial point additionally satisfies $\|y_0-y^\star(x_0)\|_2\le R_y$. The condition number is $\kappa=\beta/\mu_y$.
source_fields.parameter_domain_description: $\Delta$: positive real; $R_y$: nonnegative real; $\beta$: positive real; $d_x$: positive integer; $d_y$: positive integer; $\varepsilon$: positive real; $\mu_y$: $0<\mu_y\le\beta$; $\rho$: positive real. Derived quantities are defined in the parameter table. Additional accuracy and dimension conditions are stated in each regime.

source_fields.finiteness_conditions: Use the compact-domain, solution-existence, and smoothness assumptions in the model and the stated metric definition.
source_fields.normalization: The exact formula governs; norms, squares, maxima, and expectations are not interchanged.

source_fields.cost: vector (N_payoff_first_order,N_HVP); each selected direction costs one HVP
description_paragraphs: Public inputs include block dimensions $d_x,d_y$ and $\Delta$, $R_y$, $\beta$, $\varepsilon$, $\mu_y$, $\rho$, together with the stated initial point and feasible geometry. The analytic representation of the hidden function, operator, or matrix is not revealed.

$$

$$

$$
Every direction is charged separately. Reconstructing the complete Hessian from basis directions requires $d_x+d_y$ HVP calls.
Inner optimizers, reduced gradients, and reduced Hessians are not supplied directly. Linear algebra on returned data does not reveal new information about hidden functions.
source_fields.no_free_information: full Hessian may be reconstructed with d_x+d_y HVPs at fixed z, not one call
source_fields.operation_2: query (z,v), v in R^{d_x+d_y}: exact nabla^2 f(z) v

operations.order_convention: Derivative order refers to the scalar payoff $f$. The joint gradient has two blocks; the response signature specifies whether a Hessian or complete derivative jet is supplied.

source_fields.query_domain_description: Each operation's query_signature is the authoritative query domain. Permissions for queries outside the ball or restrictions to feasible queries are enforced separately for each interface.

source_fields.allowed_postprocessing: The output may be any measurable postprocessing of the history, including an unqueried point, average, or convex combination. It must satisfy the stated domain and feasibility requirements; no additional function value or computable certificate is required.
source_fields.certificate_requirement: No additional computable certificate is required beyond any graph element explicitly listed in the output.

description_paragraphs: Retain the joint fixed budget $(N_{\rm first},N_{\rm HVP})$; without cost weights, do not combine its coordinates into one scalar optimal rate.

The fixed joint budget $(B_{\rm first},B_{\rm HVP})$ requires $N_{\rm first}\le B_{\rm first}$ and $N_{\rm HVP}\le B_{\rm HVP}$ for every instance and execution path. Each Hessian action in a specified direction is charged separately.

Count all information calls for one instance and one requested accuracy, including initialization. Exact-real arithmetic, storage, and solving known models from public inputs and returned data are uncharged. This query-complexity quantity does not certify arithmetic or bit complexity.
source_fields.precision_model: Exact real information; internal arithmetic, storage, and bit costs are excluded from the query count.
source_fields.scalarization: Keep joint budgets when cost weights are unspecified. Project only onto an explicitly designated primary query coordinate.
source_fields.setup_cost: All charged initialization queries are included in the total budget.
